title: Admission Crediting + Attention-Windowing: adaptive prefill crediting to stabilize continuous batches
creator: Aisha Raman
body:
Background:

Current continuous-batching admission heuristics rely primarily on headroom timers and simple size thresholds. In mixed-workload clusters we observe a recurring tail-latency mode: long-running prefill-heavy requests (long context, large kv cache warmups) either monopolize kernel paths or cause frequent kernel reconfiguration churn, which increases p95/p99 for latency-sensitive short requests. Existing mitigations (static isolation, hard caps) reduce throughput or increase cost.

Goal:

Introduce an "admission crediting" mechanism combined with an attention-windowing hint that: (1) gives short low-cost requests prioritized admission credits, (2) dynamically meters prefill admissions when kernel handoffs are likely, and (3) exposes an attention-window hint so the kernel selector can prefer attention-optimized kernels for incoming batches without costly re-profiling. Expected outcomes: reduce p95 by ~15-25% for mixed workloads, reduce kernel reconfiguration frequency by >=40%, and keep aggregate throughput within 5% of baseline.

Design summary (high level):

1) Admission Crediting: each request gets a short-lived credit token budget based on estimated work (tokens, expected kv prefill). Credits are consumed by admission; short requests receive an initial boosted credit grant to favor low-latency admission. Long requests can spend credits but are rate-limited to avoid burst monopolization. Credits are tenant-aware and decay across windows to avoid starvation.

2) Attention-Window Hinting: at prefill time we compute a compact attention-window signature (seeded from prefix length, recent sequence distribution) and attach a hint to the admission record. The scheduler forwards batches that are attention-homogenous to the kernel planner, which prefers an attention-optimized kernel variant. This avoids full kernel probing for each heterogenous mini-batch.

3) Kernel Negotiator: a lightweight matching layer that uses credit and attention hints to decide whether to: (a) coalesce into an existing batch on a kernel path, (b) spawn on a shared fallback kernel, or (c) defer admission by x ms (backoff) to align shapes. The negotiator also exposes metrics to observe reconfiguration attempts.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:

- p95 token latency for 64-token short requests in mixed load decreases by >=15% measured on benchmark-mix-2025.02.
- Kernel reconfiguration rate (per-GPU per-hour) drops >=40% vs baseline for the same workload.
- No customer-facing error increase; error rate stays within baseline +0.1%.
- No single-tenant starvation observed in 72-hour soak test (fairness metrics pass).
- End-to-end throughput within 5% of current baseline for steady-state queries.

Trade-offs and open questions:

- Complexity: admission credit accounting adds state and per-tenant bookkeeping. We will store credits in the local node with opportunistic replication to avoid remote calls. This is an operational risk but keeps latency low.
- Estimation accuracy: mis-estimates of prefill cost could misallocate credits. We'll start with conservative estimates (prefix length bands) and roll out a learning component in a follow-up ticket.
- Attention signature compactness: need to balance collision risk vs utility. We propose a 32-bit hash of window parameters as initial iteration.

Implementation plan (phases):

Phase 1 (P0): Design + prototype (this ticket)
- Implement local credit ledger (node-local, tenant-scoped, expires after window).
- Add credit checks to admission path and implement short-request boosted initial grant.
- Build attention-window extractor in prefill code path and attach hint to admission envelope.
- Add negotiator stub that logs decisions and exposes debug traces.

Phase 2 (P1): Pilot + metrics
- Run pilot on dedicated canary fleet (low-traffic region).
- Add kernel reconfig counters, admission denial/retry metrics, and fairness histograms.
- Observe effects and iterate parameters (grant size, decay half-life, backoff ms).

Phase 3 (P2): Rollout + learning
- Add server-side learning to adjust credit grants by tenant and by timeseries of observed prefill cost.
- Expose runtime knobs in Console (prefill-credit-param, attention-hint-enable).

Testing plan:

- Unit tests for credit ledger, expiry, and concurrency.
- Integration test across admission path with synthetic short/long mixes.
- Soak tests for 72 hours on canary with production-like distribution.
- Chaos test for node failure with replicated ledger to ensure eventual fairness.

Rollout plan and safety knobs:

- Start on canary fleet (10% of traffic), monitor kernel-reconfig-rate and p95.
- Auto-rollback if p95 increases >5% or kernel churn increases >10% within 30 minutes of deploy.
- Feature flag gated: runtime flag engine.admission_crediting.enabled = false by default.

References / artifacts:

- Design sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/Admission+Crediting+and+Attention+Windowing
- Load spec and benchmark harness: https://internal.redwood.ai/benchmarks/mixed-workload-2025-02
- PR (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8254
- Dashboards: https://observability.redwood.ai/d/expr/batching-kernel-churn

Notes / follow-ups:

- Follow-up ticket to add learning-based credit adjustments (ENG-575422 planned).
- Consider integrating with dedicated capacity reservation signals to provide guaranteed credits for reserved instances.

2025-02-21 Review (PM): Jordan Lee: Reviewed for customer impact and agreed on pilot window. Requested that the pilot include a fairness histogram by tenant size.
